recipes.name: Spicy Indian Chicken and Mango Curry
ingredients_raw: 2 medium mangoes, peeled and sliced, divided
14 ounces skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into cubes
1 large English cucumber, seeded and sliced

steps.text: Place half of the mango slices into the bowl of a blender with the coconut milk. Blend until smooth and reserve for later.

Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Stir in the curry paste, and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the chicken and shallot; cook until the chicken is done and the shallots have softened, about 5 minutes. Pour in the mango puree, and cook until heated through. To serve, stir in the remaining mango slices and cucumber.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Indian Chicken and Mango Curry
raw_recipe.description: This delicious, Indian-inspired dish is made by quickly cooking chicken and shallots with curry paste, then bathing everything with a coconut milk-mango puree!

review.reviewBody:
It was the best curry ever!
Somewhere between korma and tikka masala.
Creamy but spicy.
But I do have one advice for anyone who is interested, DO NOT BE AFRAID TO ADD MORE SPICES!! I have made my own curry powder and I have marinaded chicken over night prior to cooking.
Here is my curry powder recipe, two servings, ENJOY!!!

3tsp Cilantro/Coriander powder
4tsp Cumin
1/2tsp Very hot chilli powder
1/2tsp Chopped ginger
1/2tsp Chopped garlic
1tsp Garlic powder
2tsp Sugar
2tsp Mixed spice (Nutmeg, Cinnamon, Ginger, Cloves, Dill seeds, Coriander)
1tsp Turmeric
2tsp Paprika powder

I was not super impressed with the original recipe. I thought it was too bland! However, the mango sounded fantastic and as a base it's a great dish. I think part of the reason why mine did not turn out as well is because the mangos that I used were not ripe enough. I will try again with super ripe mangos and see how this turns out. 
I did add garam masala to the chicken and I also threw in a little bit of sugar and minced garlic to the dish in an effort to add some flavor. I also ran out and got some fish sauce. That made it a lot tastier and the next day, the dish was even better after the flavors had mixed together. Definitely get the fish sauce and add it to the chicken while cooking then splash a little on your plate at the end. It makes a big difference. 
Also, make sure your mangos are properly ripened! I think that will add a bit of sweetness to your recipe without having to add sugar.

I made a few changes. My family really loved this and ate the whole double batch in one setting. I had to use frozen mangoes and light coconut milk (what I had in pantry). I sauteed half an onion with 1 garlic clove before adding the chicken, then sprinkled garam masala on the chicken while cooking. I added 1 T of curry powder. For garnish bowl, I chopped green onions and mixed them with leftover marinated cucumbers, drained and chopped (marinated in spicy vinegar).

This recipe is amazing! The first time I followed the recipe exactly but I found the mango overwhelmed the coconut milk flavour and the spice was bland for my tastes. The next time I reduced the mangoes to 1 and added more spice: 1 tsp chili paste, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/4 tsp garlic, 1 tsp fresh ginger, 1/2 tsp paprika. I also used half a can of coconut milk to reduce the fat the second time around. Thanks so much for such a wonderful and refreshing recipe!

My husband and I love this recipe and have made it on numerous occasions. We pretty much follow it exactly, but we also add in some pineapple (to both the sauce and actual chunks in the dish - only use a bit though because the pineapple can overtake the mango flavoring) and about a tablespoon of minced ginger. I also serve it with shredded coconut on top and use an indian-inspired rice as a base (cook your rice with browned onion and a bit of cinnamon and cumin). DEEE-LICIOUSNESS!

Very good. I made a few changes, added an additional tablespoon of the curry paste, a tbs or garam masala, and salt. Cooked the onions with a clove of garlic before first before adding the paste. I also ditched the cucumbers.

Will definitely cook it again

This is a great recipe. I added 2 cloves of chopped garlic, about 2tbs minced ginger and some mustard seed to the shallots. When the mustard seeds start to pop add the coconut milk mixture. I also added some yellow curry powder. At the end i used garam marsala. I left out the cucumber (didn't have any available) It came out just like my favorite Indian restaurants!

This is an unique recipe indeed. However 1 can of coconut milk will give a mild creamy taste to the curry instead of spicy. It will be good to cut down the coconut milk in half to bring the spiciness. I have only blended one mango and did not add any mango or cucumber slices to the meal.Moreover I have added ground cumin, tumeric powder, curry powder and garam masala. A pinch of salt will bring out the flavour and I have sprinkled ground black pepper and chilli flakes at the end. Spicy yet creamy. Perfect combo!

This dish tasted so good. It's spicy and a bit tangy because of the mangoes. My family loved it... Then I made a variation... I used firm Tofu (quickly fried on all sides just enough to make a soft brown crust) and then followed the rest of the procedure... the end result is equally delicious! This Tofu version, I made for a vegetarian friend who's a cancer survivor... He loved it!

While I didn't follow this faithfully, the results were unbelievable.

I had no fresh mango, so I went to the freezer and used a tropical fruit mix I use for smoothies, which had papaya, mango, and pineapple.

I also used half a sweet onion in place of the shallots and added sliced red bell pepper and snow peas and let them simmer in the sauce with the chicken for about ten minutes.

I did not add any seasonings, but also was fairly heavy handed with the curry paste. The balance of sweet with spicy was really, really delightful. This is going to be in the regular rotation at our house!

My family loved this. My changes were to use 3 large mangos and since I had powdered coconut I used this with some fruit juice (mango/orange) in place of the coconut milk. To kick up the colour of the sauce I added 3 tablespoons of chopped parsley into the blender. Both the color and flavor were vivid!

This was fantastic. My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed it. It was a bit much cucumber for my personal taste, but I took a few slices out and it was just perfect. It's in the permanent recipe box now. Update: I made this again tonight. I had to substitute onions and garlic for the shallots because they were what I had and I used half a cucumber. My curry paste wasn’t very spicy, so I added some crushed red pepper for kick, a dash of fish sauce for some extra umami and topped with some fresh cilantro. Thanks for sharing!

I made it using red curry paste, and garlic and onion instead of shallots. Mostly because I have a mango tree and needed to use them! I used twice as much mango. Everyone liked it!! Next time I will try it with Indian curry powder to see how it tastes different, since I wasn’t sure what curry it was calling for.

Many years ago I had a dush at an Indian restaurant that included mango. Unfortunately the restaurant closed and I've never found the dish anywhere else. My Indian friends have told me this is not a common dish. So I was excited to make this to see how it compares. It's really good but I pretty much doubled the amount of curry paste and still found it mild. But otherwise it's good and I'm sure I'll make it again. it's also much simpler to make than most Indian dishes.

It was a hit and we’ve had a similar dish at a local Indian restaurant that we loved called “Shrimp Molly”. It was a similar curry sauce with a kick of heat and sweetness and pairs well with shrimp and chicken.

Made this for the first time tonight with a 13oz can of coconut milk and Thai Kitchen green curry paste. While it was definitely tasty, the paste had zero heat. Tasted a little of the paste directly and it had little or no heat. I kinda thought green curry paste is supposed to be the hotter one?

Very good recipe, but it definitely needs more spices, in my opinion. I made this twice and stuck to the recipe exactly the first time, and then added to it the second time. I definitely recommend adding an extra mango to the blender with the coconut milk. I also used a lot more curry paste than this called for and a big dollop of pepper jelly. I think mango chutney would be excellent in this as well!
Yum it was great! I did turn up the heat a bit more with red pepper flakes and added about 2 tablespoons of fish sauce. It's a keeper!
This recipe is a good base. I would look at the other reviews where they added more spice to the recipe. Needs more spice.
just awesome
